summary: STANDARDS-axis review of riders sweep-wave-S lane 01 against 7bc5a710f. This is an unusually rigorous body of work: independently re-measured prestate/tail pins against the live lane database (clara_l04:55744) for three separate functions (_assert_plan_authority, _accrual_plan_core, _authority_ref_refusal) and all three matched the reports' claimed shas exactly; re-ran the firm-scope-db-pins corpus test (22/22 pass, confirming migrations 0330-0334 are static DDL needing no new barrier entry); confirmed the live migration ledger reads 314 files / max 0334_accrual_list_side_filter as claimed; verified the preintegration-gate chain in packages/db/package.json holds exactly 130 --import flags appended in migration order at the sorted position; verified rig-meta.mjs cohorts exist only for the three migrations that mint new names (0330, 0332, 0333) and are correctly absent for the two that don't (0331, 0334); confirmed no applied migration, no docs/PRD.md, no docs/ARCHITECTURE.md, no packages/runtime file and no frozen-workflows.json file appear anywhere in the diff; confirmed no new relations (so no FORCE RLS obligation) and that recut bodies preserve SECURITY DEFINER/search_path/owner/ACL by grep of the migration text; spot-checked TDD test files for non-tautological, independent-literal expected values; and reviewed the apps/web diffs for smell-baseline issues (duplication, feature envy, primitive obsession, speculative generality, divergent change) and found none of note -- every new helper mirrors an existing sibling convention and every shared-file hunk is minimal and at the sorted position. The one real, repeated standards deviation is CONTEXT.md: SWEEP-PLAN.md's shared-files table assigns it to 'L3 only, and only if #1049 stays in the wave,' yet this lane (L1) edited it in four separate commits, each self-disclosed but none preceded by an orchestrator ruling. Reported as minor rather than a blocker because the hunks are disjoint, factually justified, and transparently flagged for the merger in every ticket report. No hard violations of a documented standard were found, and no TDD anti-pattern (implementation-coupled test, tautological assertion, horizontal slicing, unwarranted mocking of an internal collaborator) survived inspection of the actual diffs and commit history.

findings.title: CONTEXT.md edited by L1 four times despite SWEEP-PLAN.md assigning it to L3 only
findings.evidence: docs/plan/active/riders-2026-09-20/SWEEP-PLAN.md's Shared files table: 'CONTEXT.md | L3, only if #1049 stays in the wave | A staff person record is a new domain entity and owes a CONTEXT entry.' Lane 01 is not listed as an owner of CONTEXT.md for this wave, yet `git diff 7bc5a710f...HEAD -- CONTEXT.md` shows four separate hunks landed across commits 2ada717aa (#1051), f762c1a87 (#1080), ab42ceb55 (#1074) and fc9d61b2b (#1073), inside the 'Authorising instruction', 'Plan occurrence', 'Accrual reversal', 'Accrual correction' and 'Settlement candidate row' entries. Each ticket report explicitly flags the deviation ('SWEEP-PLAN.md's shared-file table assigns CONTEXT.md to L3 only... I edited it anyway') but none sought an orchestrator ruling before landing the hunk, four times over.
findings.required_fix: Not a functional defect: the hunks are disjoint, each is a genuine correction of vocabulary this lane's own tickets made stale, and each was transparently disclosed. Still, this is a documented plan-of-record ownership rule the lane knowingly crossed four times without waiting for a ruling. The merger/orchestrator should confirm no other lane (in particular any lane touching '#1049'/L3 material) has landed a colliding CONTEXT.md hunk before integrating, and this pattern should not become the house norm for future waves without an explicit exception in the plan of record.

findings.title: Lint-avoidance rename of test titles in #1073 (cosmetic, verified benign)
findings.evidence: apps/web/components/firm/accrual-bill-conflict-affordance.test.tsx: two test titles containing the literal string '#1073' were reworded to 'ticket 1073' because the raw-colour-selector lint rule matched the '#' + hex-like digits inside a string literal. Ticket #1073's report calls this out as a known lint false-positive and names the fix as the rule's own recommended workaround.
findings.required_fix: None required. Verified this is a title-only rename with no assertion weakened (the rewritten test gained more coverage, not less). Recorded only because a rename to dodge a lint rule deserves a second look; on inspection it is exactly what it claims to be.
